accepted.s:
Which of the following sets comprises governance reforms aimed at reducing the size and cost of the State?
1. Downsizing the bureaucracy
2. Disinvestment
3. Privatisation of higher educational institutions
4. Encouraging foreign direct investment inflows
accepted.x: Downsizing, disinvestment and privatisation of higher educational institutions reduce the size or direct role of the State. Encouraging FDI is primarily a growth and external-sector measure, not a downsizing measure.
accepted.tq: Separate measures that reduce State ownership from broader growth and external-sector measures.
accepted.sec: Downsizing and governance reform measures; Pay Commissions on staff strength (Fifth, Sixth, Seventh)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Disinvestment is best described as
o: the sale of part of a public-sector undertaking's equity to the public
the complete abolition of public-sector enterprises
the transfer of all government employees to private firms
the withdrawal of foreign investment from the economy
accepted.x: Disinvestment involves selling part of a public-sector undertaking's equity to the public. It need not involve complete transfer of ownership or management.
accepted.tq: Distinguish partial equity sale from complete privatisation.
accepted.sec: Downsizing and governance reform measures; Pay Commissions on staff strength (Fifth, Sixth, Seventh)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Public-sector employment declined from approximately 19.6 million in 1991 to 17.5 million in 2008 mainly because
o: all public-sector enterprises were converted into departments
the number of government departments was doubled
uncompetitive public-sector enterprises closed or downsized
accepted.x: Public-sector employment fell from 19.6 million in 1991 to 17.5 million in 2008 as uncompetitive public-sector enterprises closed or downsized.
accepted.tq: Link the numerical trend with its stated structural cause.
accepted.sec: Downsizing and governance reform measures; Pay Commissions on staff strength (Fifth, Sixth, Seventh)  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Fifth Central Pay Commission was chaired by
accepted.x: The Fifth Pay Commission was chaired by Justice S. Ratnavel Pandian in 1997.
accepted.tq: Match the commission with its chairperson rather than its year alone.
accepted.sec: Downsizing and governance reform measures; Pay Commissions on staff strength (Fifth, Sixth, Seventh)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the staff-strength recommendation associated with the Fifth Pay Commission?
o: Merger of Group D into Group C and introduction of running pay bands
Introduction of performance-linked pay and rationalisation of allowances
Replacement of pay bands by a pay matrix
A reduction of staff strength by about 30% and a freeze on new posts
accepted.x: The Fifth Pay Commission recommended cutting staff strength by about 30% and imposing a freeze on new posts.
accepted.tq: Use commission-specific staff-structure details to avoid interchange of neighbouring commissions.
accepted.sec: Downsizing and governance reform measures; Pay Commissions on staff strength (Fifth, Sixth, Seventh)  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Pay Commission)
A. Fifth Pay Commission
B. Sixth Pay Commission
C. Seventh Pay Commission

List-II (Feature)
1. Pay matrix replaced pay bands
2. Group D merged into Group C
3. Staff strength cut by about 30%

Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Fifth Commission was associated with a 30% staff-strength cut, the Sixth with merger of Group D into Group C, and the Seventh with replacement of pay bands by a pay matrix.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive commission-feature pairs and eliminate swapped codes.
accepted.sec: Downsizing and governance reform measures; Pay Commissions on staff strength (Fifth, Sixth, Seventh)  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

1. Fifth Pay Commission — Justice S. Ratnavel Pandian — 1997
2. Sixth Pay Commission — Justice B.N. Srikrishna — 2008
3. Seventh Pay Commission — Justice A.K. Mathur — 2015
4. Seventh Pay Commission — effective from 2015
accepted.x: The Seventh Pay Commission was chaired in 2015 but its recommendations were effective from 2016, not 2015. The other pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Check the distinction between the commission year and the year its recommendations became effective.
accepted.sec: Downsizing and governance reform measures; Pay Commissions on staff strength (Fifth, Sixth, Seventh)  [other exams]

accepted.s:
The Sixth Pay Commission is associated with which of the following combinations?
1. Merger of Group D into Group C
2. Introduction of running pay bands
3. Performance Related Incentive Scheme
4. Rationalisation of allowances
accepted.x: The Sixth Pay Commission introduced the merger of Group D into Group C, running pay bands and the Performance Related Incentive Scheme. Rationalisation of allowances is associated with the Seventh Commission.
accepted.tq: Separate adjacent commission recommendations by identifying the transferred feature.
accepted.sec: Downsizing and governance reform measures; Pay Commissions on staff strength (Fifth, Sixth, Seventh)  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following was associated with the Seventh Pay Commission?
1. Pay matrix replacing pay bands
2. Performance-linked pay
3. Rationalisation of allowances
4. Freeze on new posts
accepted.x: The Seventh Pay Commission introduced a pay matrix in place of pay bands, performance-linked pay and rationalised allowances. The freeze on new posts belonged to the Fifth Commission.
accepted.tq: Find the one recommendation belonging to an earlier commission.
accepted.sec: Downsizing and governance reform measures; Pay Commissions on staff strength (Fifth, Sixth, Seventh)  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 proposed redefining a Government Company in a manner that would permit the State to hold
accepted.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 proposed a definition under which the State could hold less than 51%, indicating a new paradigm for disinvestment.
accepted.tq: Focus on the changed ownership threshold rather than the conventional controlling-share figure.
accepted.sec: Downsizing and governance reform measures; Pay Commissions on staff strength (Fifth, Sixth, Seventh)  [other exams]

accepted.s: New Public Management primarily brought which element into government administration?
o: Complete replacement of public services by voluntary organisations
accepted.x: New Public Management brought private-sector techniques into government, including performance auditing, contracting out and customer-oriented service delivery.
accepted.tq: Identify the defining administrative shift rather than an extreme consequence.
accepted.sec: New Public Management - originators, core principles, pioneering countries

accepted.s:
Which of the following are characteristic features of New Public Management?
1. Performance auditing
2. Contracting out non-core services
3. Treating the citizen as a customer
4. Rejection of all performance measures
accepted.x: NPM promotes performance auditing, contracting out non-core services and a customer-oriented view of citizens. It does not reject performance measurement.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the performance-oriented character of NPM.
accepted.sec: New Public Management - originators, core principles, pioneering countries

accepted.s: The term ‘New Public Management’ was popularised by
accepted.x: Christopher Hood popularised the term New Public Management in 1991.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the originator of the term from authors of related reform theories.
accepted.sec: New Public Management - originators, core principles, pioneering countries

accepted.s:
Which one of the following sets contains the pioneering countries associated with New Public Management?
1. United Kingdom
2. New Zealand
3. Australia
4. United States of America
accepted.x: The United Kingdom under Thatcher, New Zealand, Australia and the United States are identified as pioneering countries of NPM.
accepted.tq: Use the complete country set and avoid excluding a country merely because one is especially prominent.
accepted.sec: New Public Management - originators, core principles, pioneering countries

accepted.s:
Which of the following is NOT a doctrine associated with Christopher Hood’s New Public Management?
1. Hands-on professional management
2. Explicit standards and performance measures
3. Emphasis on output controls
4. Complete elimination of competition in the public sector
accepted.x: NPM includes hands-on management, explicit performance standards, output controls and competition in the public sector. It does not call for complete elimination of competition.
accepted.tq: Locate the statement that directly reverses an NPM doctrine.
accepted.sec: New Public Management - originators, core principles, pioneering countries

accepted.s: Disaggregation into smaller units or agencies, competition in the public sector, private-sector management styles, and discipline and parsimony in resource use are associated with
accepted.x: These are among Christopher Hood’s stated NPM doctrines, along with professional management, performance measures and output controls.
accepted.tq: Recognise a cluster of doctrines rather than relying on a single keyword.
accepted.sec: New Public Management - originators, core principles, pioneering countries

accepted.s: Who authored the book Reinventing Government (1992)?
o: Justice B.N. Srikrishna and Justice A.K. Mathur
accepted.x: Reinventing Government, published in 1992, was authored by David Osborne and Ted Gaebler.
accepted.tq: Match the book with its authors, not with theorists of later critiques.
accepted.sec: Reinventing Government - authors and ten principles

accepted.s: The catchphrase associated with Reinventing Government is
accepted.x: Reinventing Government uses the catchphrase “steering, not rowing,” signifying that government should guide rather than directly perform every service function.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the similar phrases ‘steering, not rowing’ and ‘serve, not steer’.
accepted.sec: Reinventing Government - authors and ten principles

accepted.s:
Match the following principles of Reinventing Government with their meanings:

A. Catalytic
B. Community-owned
C. Competitive
D. Mission-driven

1. Empower rather than serve
2. Inject competition into service delivery
3. Steer rather than row
4. Move from rules to mission

Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Catalytic government steers rather than rows; community-owned government empowers; competitive government injects competition; mission-driven government moves from rules to mission.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive ‘steer rather than row’ pair and then resolve the remaining matches.
accepted.sec: Reinventing Government - authors and ten principles

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Results-oriented — fund outcomes, not inputs
2. Customer-driven — meet the needs of the customer, not the bureaucracy
3. Enterprising — earn rather than spend
4. Anticipatory — prevent rather than cure
accepted.x: All four pairs correctly state principles of Reinventing Government: results-oriented, customer-driven, enterprising and anticipatory administration.
accepted.tq: Verify each principle against its precise contrast rather than selecting a partial set.
accepted.sec: Reinventing Government - authors and ten principles

accepted.s: In the Reinventing Government framework, moving from hierarchy to participation and teamwork is the meaning of which principle?
accepted.x: The decentralised principle seeks to move from hierarchy to participation and teamwork.
accepted.tq: Match the organisational contrast with the corresponding principle.
accepted.sec: Reinventing Government - authors and ten principles

accepted.s: Leveraging change through the market is associated with which principle of Reinventing Government?
accepted.x: The market-oriented principle seeks to leverage change through the market.
accepted.tq: Identify the principle from its distinctive market-based objective.
accepted.sec: Reinventing Government - authors and ten principles

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?

1. Catalytic — steer rather than row
2. Community-owned — empower rather than serve
3. Customer-driven — fund outcomes, not inputs
4. Anticipatory — prevent rather than cure
accepted.x: ‘Fund outcomes, not inputs’ is the results-oriented principle. Customer-driven government focuses on meeting the needs of the customer rather than the bureaucracy.
accepted.tq: Spot the swapped meaning between two neighbouring principles.
accepted.sec: Reinventing Government - authors and ten principles

accepted.s: The New Public Service approach was developed by
o: Justice S. Ratnavel Pandian and Justice A.K. Mathur
accepted.x: The New Public Service approach is associated with Denhardt and Denhardt, published in 2000.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the authors of a critique of NPM from the authors of Reinventing Government.
accepted.sec: New Public Service and Public Value theory → author, as critiques of NPM

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the New Public Service approach:
1. It emphasises democratic citizenship and community building.
2. It places public interest above market efficiency.
3. Its central prescription is that administrators should serve, not steer.
4. It reduces the citizen to a customer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: New Public Service emphasises democratic citizenship, community building, public interest and serving rather than steering. Reducing the citizen to a customer is a feature criticised by New Public Service, not its own position.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that attributes the NPM view of the citizen to its critique.
accepted.sec: New Public Service and Public Value theory → author, as critiques of NPM

accepted.s: Who wrote Creating Public Value (1995)?
accepted.x: Mark Moore wrote Creating Public Value in 1995 and developed the Public Value perspective.
accepted.tq: Match the title and year with the theorist of Public Value.
accepted.sec: New Public Service and Public Value theory → author, as critiques of NPM

accepted.s: Which of the following best expresses the core claim of Public Value theory?
o: Public managers should pursue efficiency alone, irrespective of legitimacy
Government should withdraw entirely from public service delivery
Public managers create value for the public, including legitimacy and trust
Citizens should be treated exclusively as customers of government
accepted.x: Public Value theory holds that managers create value for the public, including legitimacy and trust, and not merely efficiency.
accepted.tq: Apply the theory to distinguish public value from narrow market efficiency.
accepted.sec: New Public Service and Public Value theory → author, as critiques of NPM

accepted.s: New Public Service and Public Value theory have in common that they
o: reject legitimacy and trust as administrative concerns
reject the reduction of citizens to customers and the State to a service seller
treat market efficiency as the only public objective
support the complete replacement of government by private firms
accepted.x: Both approaches critique NPM’s reduction of the citizen to a customer and of the State to a service seller.
accepted.tq: Identify the shared critique rather than a claim belonging exclusively to one theory.
accepted.sec: New Public Service and Public Value theory → author, as critiques of NPM

accepted.s: Outsourcing in public administration refers to
o: selling all government-owned land to the public
transferring legislative powers to private companies
hiring regular services from external sources that were earlier performed in-house
appointing only permanent government employees through competitive examinations
accepted.x: Outsourcing involves hiring external sources for services such as legal, IT, advertising and security work previously performed in-house.
accepted.tq: Use the distinction between external service procurement and permanent public employment.
accepted.sec: Contractualisation and outsourcing - contract employees in government, APCOS

accepted.s: The growth of outsourcing was particularly facilitated by
o: the reduction of all contractual employment
the decline of information technology and communication
accepted.x: Outsourcing grew with the development of information technology and fast communication.
accepted.tq: Link the administrative trend to its stated technological enablers.
accepted.sec: Contractualisation and outsourcing - contract employees in government, APCOS

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding unionisation and contract labour is correct?
1. Only 6.3% of the workforce is unionised.
2. Unionisation in the private sector is 1.8%.
3. The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 requires 10% or 100 workers to form a union.
4. Since 1991, all organised-sector workers have maintained a direct relation with their employer.

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: The workforce unionisation rate is 6.3%, the private-sector rate is 1.8%, and the Industrial Relations Code 2020 uses the threshold of 10% or 100 workers. Contractualisation has weakened direct employer relations for many organised-sector workers, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Check the numerical thresholds and reject the absolute statement reversing the effect of contractualisation.
accepted.sec: Contractualisation and outsourcing - contract employees in government, APCOS

accepted.s: Contract labour constituted what share of the manufacturing workforce in 2022-23?
accepted.x: Contract labour constituted 40.7% of the manufacturing workforce in 2022-23, compared with 20% in 1999.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the current share from the earlier benchmark and the separate productivity figure.
accepted.sec: Contractualisation and outsourcing - contract employees in government, APCOS

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the trend in contract labour in manufacturing?
1. It increased from 20% in 1999 to 40.7% in 2022-23.
2. Contract-labour-intensive firms showed 31% lower productivity.
3. The trend indicates a complete disappearance of contractual employment.

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Contract labour increased from 20% in 1999 to 40.7% in 2022-23, while contract-labour-intensive firms showed 31% lower productivity. It did not disappear; statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Separate the direction of a trend from an extreme and unsupported conclusion.
accepted.sec: Contractualisation and outsourcing - contract employees in government, APCOS

accepted.s: APCOS stands for
o: Administrative Public Contracting and Operations Service
accepted.x: APCOS means AP Corporation for Outsourced Services.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of an official institutional acronym.
accepted.sec: Contractualisation and outsourcing - contract employees in government, APCOS

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly describes APCOS?
1. It was set up by the Andhra Pradesh Government in 2020.
2. It recruits outsourced staff.
3. It pays outsourced staff directly.
4. It retains contractor middlemen as the essential link in payment.

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: APCOS was set up by the Andhra Pradesh Government in 2020 to recruit outsourced staff and pay them directly, thereby cutting out contractor middlemen. Statement 4 is therefore false.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional purpose and reject the statement that reverses its payment function.
accepted.sec: Contractualisation and outsourcing - contract employees in government, APCOS

accepted.s: Approximately how many outsourced APSRTC employees are paid through contractors and reportedly face issues relating to wages, PF and ESI?
accepted.x: About 8,000 outsourced APSRTC employees are paid through contractors and face irregularities involving wages, provident fund and ESI; they have demanded equal pay.
accepted.tq: Read the magnitude carefully and connect it with the associated employment issues.
accepted.sec: Contractualisation and outsourcing - contract employees in government, APCOS

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding NEDCAP is correct?
o: NEDCAP stopped recruiting staff after 1987 because of APCOS.
All staff recruited after 1987 were immediately made permanent employees.
NEDCAP recruited only foreign consultants after 1987.
Staff recruited after 1987 were retained only as contract or outsourced workers.
accepted.x: At NEDCAP, staff recruited after 1987 were kept only as contract or outsourced workers.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the stated employment status from permanent appointment and non-recruitment claims.
accepted.sec: Contractualisation and outsourcing - contract employees in government, APCOS
